prerequisites: Basic notions of high school mathematics courses (formal calculus, polynomials, algebraic equations and inequalities, elements of analytic geometry, and trigonometry)

learning_outcomes.text: Development of an adequate expression and technical discussion of own arguments.
Knowledge and understanding of both mathematical principles and the role of mathematical sciences as a tool for the analysis and the problem solving of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge of the principles of computer science and the algorithmic and numerical approach to problems.

Acquisition of a good disposition to the theoretical approach and to the logical-formal rigor through the elaboration of some concepts of differential and integral calculus in one variable, improving students' skills concerning calculation techniques.

Acquisition of a good disposition to the theoretical approach and to the logical-formal rigor through the elaboration of some concepts of differential and integral calculus in one and several variables, improving students' skills concerning calculation techniques.

syllabus_topics: Sets (union, intersection, difference, empty set, complementary)
The real numbers: algebraic axioms, ordering, logical quantifiers
Maximum, minimum, upper and lower bounds, greatest lower bound and least upper bound
Property of completeness of the reals
Applications between sets, injective, surjective, bijective applications
Domain, codomain, image and graphic of an application
Main transcendent functions (exponential and logarithmic functions, trigonometric functions and their inverses, hyperbolic functions)
Elements of topology of the real line: neighborhood of a point, accumulation points, isolated points
Absolute and relative maxima and minima
Theorem of the permanence of the sign
Theorem on operations for calculating limits
Theorem of existence of the limit for monotone functions
Continuity theorems (sum, product, quotient and composition of functions)
Theorem of intermediate values and applications
Theorem on the continuity of an inverse function
Rules of derivation (sum, product, quotient, composition and inverse function)
Sufficient conditions for the existence of relative maximums and minimums
Taylor's formula with the remainder in the form of Peano
Formula of Taylor with the remainder in the form of Lagrange
Applications of the Taylor’s formula to the calculation of limits and to some approximation problems
Integration by parts of indefinite integrals
Integration by substitution for indefinite integrals
Integration of elementary functions or deduced from elementary functions
Negligible sets and necessary and sufficient conditions for integrability
Properties of definite integrals (linearity, monotonicity, additivity)
Integration by parts for definite integrals
Integration by substitution for definite integrals
Definition of the logarithm through the integral
Application of the definite integrals to the calculation of areas of plane figures and to the calculation of volumes of rotation solids
Convergence criteria (comparison, asymptotic comparison, absolute convergence)
Lower bound and upper bound of a sequence
Existence theorem of the limit for monotone sequences
The number e as limit of a sequence
Equivalent definitions of the convergence of a function, main theorem and some applications
N-th root, factorial and calculation of some limits connected to these notions
Harmonic series and generalized harmonic series
Partial and directional derivatives, continuity and differentiability, free and constrained extrema
Method of separation of variables and linear equations
Elements of topology in R^k (neighborhoods of a point, accumulation points, isolated points, interior points, boundary points, closed sets, open sets, closure and boundary of a set)
Real functions of two or more real variables
Necessary condition for extreme points (Fermat's theorem)
Finding absolute maxima and minima in closed and limited interiors
Polar, spherical, cylindrical coordinates and their Jacobians
Negligible sets in R^2 and necessary and sufficient condition for integrability in a rectangle
Integral in a limited set of R^2
Applications of double integrals to the calculation of masses, centers of mass and moments of inertia
Calculation of the integral of the Gauss function through double integrals
Negligible sets in R^3 and necessary and sufficient condition for integrability
Integral in a limited set of R^3
Reduction formulas for triple integrals (the "spaghetti" and "slices" formulas)
Change of variables formula for triple integrals
Applications of triple integrals to the calculation of masses and centers of mass
Exponential form of a complex number
Existence and uniqueness theorem (of the maximal solution of the Cauchy problem)
Integration of first-order linear equations with continuous coefficients
Integration of second-order linear differential equations with constant coefficients
Methods of variation of constants and other practical methods for determining a particular solution of non-homogeneous linear equations
Closed curves, simple curves, support of a curve
Definition of undirected curvilinear integral and its properties of linearity, monotonicity, additivity
Theorem for reducing an undirected curvilinear integral to a simple integral
Change of parameter and equivalent curve
Independence theorem of the undirected integral from parametrization
Applications to the calculation of mass, centers of mass and moments of inertia of a wire
Irrotational fields and their relationship to conservative fields
Green's formulas, Gauss's divergence theorem, and Stokes's curl theorem in the plane
Surfaces in space, regular surfaces, surface elements, surface integrals, tangent planes, and normal unit vectors
Gauss and Stokes's theorems in space
teaching_methods: Frontal teaching consisting of theory lessons and exercises done by the teacher
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and a subsequent oral exam. For the entire course, exams include a written test of Analysis 1, an oral test of Analysis 1, a written test of Analysis 2, and then a subsequent oral test of Analysis 2 (optional for Partition B034604-E-N). The student must develop the capability in applying and understanding mathematical methods to model, analyze and solve engineering problems. Students may take the written examination in Analysis 2 only after passing the oral examination in Analysis 1 (for Partition B034605-A-D).
